newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan buys about 64,350 tonnes of rice.
newsitem.headline: Japan buys about 64,350 tonnes of rice.

text.p: Japan's Food Agency said it bought 64,350 tonnes of rice in an import tender on Thursday, fulfiling its obligations for this fiscal year under a global trade pact.
It said it bought 31,000 tonnes from the United States, 10,000 from China, 10,000 from Australia and 13,350 from Thailand.
In a General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade deal in 1993, Japan agreed to gradually open its rice market. It pledged to buy 455,000 tonnes of foreign rice in fiscal 1996/97, which ends on March 31.
The agency, the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry, is Japan's sole importer of rice, wheat and barley. A Food Agency official said the average buying price was 70,420 yen per tonne.
It was the last import tender by the agency for the current fiscal year, the official said.
